pages.title: Custom Loading Video
pages.text: $(warn)Requires NarutoLoading.$()$(br2)While on the main menu or a loading screen (i.e. no world is currently loaded), drag a video file into the Minecraft window to replace NarutoLoading's background video with your chosen file.$(br2)The change takes effect immediately — no restart required.

pages.title: Trigger Conditions
pages.text: This drop handler fires when $(bold)all$() of the following are true:$(br2)• No world is currently loaded ($(bold)player == null$() and $(bold)level == null$())$(br)• NarutoLoading is installed and available$(br2)$(note)If you are inside a world, dragging a video will instead try to trigger the video cape or video screen handlers, not this one.$()

pages.title: File Handling
pages.text: $(bold)1.$() The source video is $(bold)copied$() to $(bold)config/narutoloading-sources/<hash>/$() using the source path's hash code as the folder name. The original file is not moved or deleted.$(br2)$(bold)2.$() NarutoLoading's config is updated: $(bold)videoFileName$() is set to the new path, and $(bold)audioFileName$() is reset to a blank audio placeholder.$(br2)$(bold)3.$() The environment is rebuilt via $(bold)BaseEnv.setupEnv()$() and the renderer is restarted.

pages.title: Notes
pages.text: • This handler always $(bold)returns false$(), meaning it never consumes the drop event. Subsequent handlers (e.g. video cape) will still be checked even if this handler ran successfully.$(br2)• Each drop $(bold)overwrites$() the previously configured loading video.$(br2)• The same source path will not be copied again if the target folder already exists, avoiding duplicate files.
